tasks.short: Establish and uphold appropriate classroom routines

steps.what: Establish behavior rules and order-maintaining procedures suited to the preschool children's actual needs
inputs: actual children's needs and classroom context

steps.what: Explain, model and enforce behavior rules and procedures while maintaining order among the students
outputs: guided classroom behavior and maintained routines

tasks.design: Keep classroom rule-setting and responsive enforcement with the teacher. A routine library in {LMS} cannot decide what is appropriate for the actual children or remove live guidance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rules must fit the children's needs and be applied in context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing resource libraries offer examples without replacing contextual judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguish an access or communication difficulty from a behavior issue.
tasks.human_edge: Maintain predictable routines with patient, proportionate responses.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: classroom routines and behavior guidance require responses suited to actual children's needs.

assumptions: Boundary covers establishment and live enforcement, including routines explained to children. The statement establishes no separate written policy, behavior log or send; no administrative baseline is invented.
Inputs are actual children and existing school expectations, not a new structured behavior dataset. Native resources do not remove either human step.
Shares are illustrative and fully retained; no software change means zero upkeep.
unknowns: Whether local rule-setting includes a separately authored accessible rule card
research_questions: Observe any actual rule-card or behavior-record write and separate it from live guidance if present.

incremental.description: No introduced software or recording work

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Both rule establishment and responsive enforcement remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor staff adherence to special education requirements

steps.what: Read the applicable special education program requirements for the activities being observed
Observe teachers or teacher assistants and compare actual work with special education program requirements
outputs: teacher's observed adherence and issues requiring attention

steps.what: Clarify observed practice with the staff member and give appropriate corrective guidance
inputs: teacher's observed adherence and issues requiring attention

tasks.design: Configure native current-version bookmarks in {DOCS} for the approved program requirements. The teacher still observes actual practice and discusses corrections; no worker scoring, camera monitoring or invented supervision report is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the applicable current requirement can interrupt observation preparation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document references can reduce navigation slightly.
tasks.still_hard: An observed action can have a context that the observer initially misses.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret practice fairly and clarify before correcting.

ambition.what: No broader monitoring span or automated staff judgement.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-4; program document access and applicable consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native references can assist requirement lookup but cannot determine actual staff adherence.

assumptions: Boundary includes requirement lookup, observation and feedback. No separate monitoring record or send is established by the task statement.
Program owner supplies approved requirements with version and scope; teacher selects the actual activity in s1 and observes staff in s2. Missing context is clarified in s3, not inferred from data.
Native bookmarks first. Shares are provisional; only 5% of lookup time changes. Gross 0.75 minus 0.2 upkeep gives 0.55 net; observation and feedback remain fully retained.
unknowns: Current requirement-navigation effort and local monitoring documentation
research_questions: Does a current-version bookmark save any lookup without obscuring activity-specific requirements?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if requirements are already directly available; up to 0.3% with smaller lookup gains than central 0.55% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Administer developmental tests and record actual responses

steps.what: Check the authorized test instructions, child identity and required access arrangements
inputs: existing child record and access requirements
outputs: confirmed test conditions and applicable instructions

steps.what: Administer the test to help determine the child's developmental level, needs or potential while observing actual responses
inputs: confirmed test conditions and applicable instructions
outputs: teacher-observed actual test responses and administration limitations

steps.what: Record and finish checking the actual responses, administration conditions and limitations on the test record
inputs: teacher-observed actual test responses and administration limitations

steps.what: Save the completed test record in the same pupil record system

tasks.design: Configure native child and test identifier fields in the pupil record system {OPS_SYSTEM}, retaining the actual instructions in {DOCS}. The teacher administers the test and records the actual responses, finishes checking the entry and saves it; no scoring, diagnosis or placement decision is automated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated record identifiers add typing after actual testing.
tasks.enabler_now: Native test-record forms can reuse existing child and test IDs.
tasks.still_hard: A response can reflect an access barrier rather than developmental ability.
tasks.human_edge: Administer consistently and describe limitations without over-interpreting them.

ambition.what: No automatic developmental assessment or increased testing volume.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-7; pupil-data access and applicable school consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: pupil-record forms can reuse identifiers while actual developmental test administration and response recording remain teacher work.

assumptions: OPS_SYSTEM is the pupil record system. Boundary includes protocol check, actual administration, response recording and save. No generated mark, developmental diagnosis or education-level decision is performed.

Test owner supplies authorized instructions and test version; school supplies child ID and existing access requirements. Teacher produces actual response and limitation data in s2 and enters it in s3. Missing responses remain missing, not inferred.
Native forms first. Shares are provisional; entry reduction applies only to repeated identifiers and headings. Checking stays inside normal recording rather than a new self-approval step.
Same-system save is 1% fully retained. Gross 1.9 minus 0.3 upkeep leaves 1.6 net. Any edited response requires another record check.
unknowns: Current test-record forms and actual repeated-identifier entry effort
research_questions: Can native forms reduce metadata typing without altering standardized administration or actual response records?

already_counted.description: Record and check actual test responses

incremental.description: Maintain child/test identifier fields and version choices

approvals.approved_version: complete checked test record at end of s3; edits void check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if identifiers already populate natively; up to 1% with smaller entry gains than central 1.6% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach independence and self-advocacy through practice

steps.what: Teach personal development skills such as goal setting, independence and self-advocacy through supported preschool activities and responsive practice
inputs: current learning activity and agreed support approach
outputs: supported practice of personal development skills

tasks.design: Keep responsive personal-development teaching with the teacher. Example activities in {LMS} cannot replace noticing when a child needs support to make a choice or communicate a preference.
tasks.previous_blocker: Independence and self-advocacy develop through actual supported interaction.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing activity resources provide examples without doing the teaching.
tasks.still_hard: Support participation without substituting the adult's choice for the child's.
tasks.human_edge: Respond patiently to the child's actual communication.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: teaching preschool independence and self-advocacy requires contextual adult support during practice.

assumptions: Boundary is the specified personal-development teaching. No separate progress report, goal record write or send is established, so no administrative baseline is added.
Inputs are actual child participation and existing activity context; no new structured capture is required. Native activity resources do not replace the live teaching.
No software change means zero upkeep; the whole task remains retained.
unknowns: Whether local teaching includes a separately authored progress or goal entry
research_questions: Observe and separate any actual progress write before reassessing a zero-saving conclusion.

incremental.description: No introduced software or recording process

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Actual personal-development instruction stays fully retained; no separate written workload is established.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Teachers retain responsive instruction, staff observation and test administration; native references and metadata fields offer limited assistance.
skills_to_grow: Preserve actual child responses and test limitations
Keep contextual staff observation separate from automated judgement
role.ambitious_version: Accurate source-grounded records alongside patient, responsive preschool instruction.
